'''''Goeppertia majestica''''' (syn. ''Calathea majestica''), the '''majestic prayer plant''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Marantaceae]]''. It is native to Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Guyana, and northern Brazil, and has been introduced to Venezuela.<ref name="60461040-2">{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:60461040-2 |title=''Goeppertia majestica'' (Linden) Borchs. & S.Suárez |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=7 May 2021 }}</ref> ''Goeppertia majestica'' belongs to one of the groups of Goeppertia called the Ornata Group.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=1995 |title=Will the real Calathea ornata stand up? |url=https://www.heliconia.org/_files/ugd/ef1aa2_66186af9be254c7f91b66f0220f67161.pdf |journal=Heliconia Society International Bulletin |volume=7 (3) |pages=12–16}}</ref>

== Uses ==
In the Amazon, the leaves of ''G. majestica'' (referred to as ''Calathea gigas'') are traditionally used for lining baskets for holding fish, and as thatch.<ref name="AED">{{cite book |last1=Duke |first1=James A. |last2=Vasquez |first2=Rodolfo |title=Amazonian Ethnobotanical Dictionary |date=1994 |publisher=CRC Press |page=36}}</ref>

As an ornamental, ''G. majestica'' has attractive foliage and can be grown both indoors and in outdoor gardens.<ref name="SG Albolineata">{{cite web |title=Goeppertia majestica 'Albolineata' |url=https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/1/7/1752 |website=Flora & Fauna Web |access-date=20 April 2025}}</ref>

A large member of its genus, it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Goeppertia majestica'' majestic prayer plant |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/357219/Goeppertia-majestica/Details |date=2021 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=7 May 2021 }}</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Pincel (Calathea ornata) - Inflorescencia (14914704091).jpg|left|thumb|Inflorescence of ''Goeppertia majestica'']]
''Goeppertia majestica'' has wide, long green leaves with a pink or white striped pattern on the upper side of the leaf. The pattern often disappear on mature leaves. The bottom side of the leaves can vary from purple to green and each leaf is hold by a tall and thick [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]. The [[inflorescence]] of ''Goeppertia majestica'' is made of multiple yellow [[Bract|bracts]] on a [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]]. The [[Flower|flowers]] colors are cream and purple.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Vásquez Martínez |first=Rodolfo |title=Flora del Río Cenepa, Amazonas, Perú v. 114 pt.2 |last2=Rojas Gonzáles |first2=Rocío |last3=Henk van Der |first3=Werff |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden Press |location=St. Louis, Mo. |year=2010 |pages=931 |url=https://archive.org/details/mobot31753003670434}}</ref>

== A confusion... ==
''Goeppertia majestica'' is often sold as Pin-stripe Calathea or [[Goeppertia ornata|Calathea ornata]]. While this species do exist, the plant that is sold around the world is either [[Goeppertia sanderiana]] or ''Goeppertia majestica'' The real [[Goeppertia ornata]] is a very rare striped pattern species of Goeppertia native to Venezuela and Colombia and disappeared from cultivation some time prior to the mid-1990s.<ref name=":0" />
